tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: During the year, the Company engaged in related party transactions under Section 40A(2)(b) of the Act amounting to Rs. 2,49,29,470, which was well below the threshold limit of Rs. 5 crores prescribed under the Act. This was duly disclosed in Clause 23 of the tax audit report. However, the tax officer contended that the Company had entered into specified domestic transactions (SDTs) exceeding Rs. 5 crores, i.e., Rs. 5,08,70,000. Consequently, the matter was referred to the Transfer Pricing Officer (TPO). While the TPO did not draw any adverse inference in his order, he concluded that the alleged SDTs exceeded the threshold limit by considering transactions with entities having both direct and indirect shareholding in the Company, whereas the law requires exclusion of transactions involving indirect shareholding. Accordingly, a penalty under Section 271G was levied for failure to furnish the required information.
tax_litigation.status: Appeal filed by the company has been allowed by CIT (A) vide order dated September 29, 2025. Accordingly, the penalty imposed by the AO u/s 271G of Rs. 10,17,400/- has been set aside.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Hon’ble High Court, vide order dated January 29, 2025, set aside the order of the ITAT, holding that the ITAT could not have disregarded the decision of the Special Bench and had not correctly defined the scope of adjudication while remitting the matter to the Assessing Officer (AO). The High Court held that the AO must first determine whether the undertaking given by the Company constitutes an international transaction under section 92B of the Income tax Act, 1961, after providing an opportunity of hearing to the Company. Reference to the Transfer Pricing Officer (TPO) would be made only if such determination is reached. Accordingly, the draft assessment order and the TPO orders passed pursuant to the ITAT remand were set aside. Pursuant thereto, the Company filed its response to the departmental queries. The AO, vide order dated September 24, 2025, disposed of the objections and referred the matter to the TPO. The TPO passed an order under section 92CA dated December 2, 2025 proposing a transfer pricing adjustment of ₹6,27,07,932. Subsequently, the AO passed a draft assessment order dated December 19, 2025.
tax_litigation.status: The Company has received the final assessment order dated January 27, 2026 passed under section 143(3) read with section 144C(3) of the Income tax Act, 1961, wherein an addition of Rs. 6.26 crore has been made on account of fee for undertaking a corporate guarantee. The Company has filed an appeal against the said order before the Commissioner of Income tax (Appeals). The Assessing Officer has raised a demand of Rs. 443.28 crore. tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The appeal relates to Assessment Year (AY) 2008-09 and was filed by the Company under Section 260A of the Income-tax Act, challenging the order dated 16 June 2020 passed by the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) in ITA Nos. 3865 & 3996/Del./2014. The Company has contested the ITAT's decision to remand the matter to the Assessing Officer (AO)/Transfer Pricing Officer (TPO) for fresh consideration of the transfer pricing adjustment pertaining to the alleged corporate guarantee issued by the Company to facilitate overseas fund raising by its subsidiary, NNPLC. Notice has been issued to the Revenue, and the substantial questions of law are yet to be admitted by the Court. Pursuant to the Court's order dated 11 January 2022, the TPO has been permitted to continue the remand proceedings; however, the AO has been restrained from passing the final assessment order pending further directions.
tax_litigation.status: Pursuant to the judgment dated January 29, 2025, the Hon'ble High Court set aside the ITAT’s order, holding that the ITAT could not have disregarded the order of the Special Bench. While disposing of the appeal, the High Court observed that the ITAT, while remanding the matter to the Assessing Officer (AO), had not correctly defined the scope of adjudication. Accordingly, the High Court directed that the AO must first determine whether the undertaking provided by the Company constitutes an international transaction under Section 92B of the Income-tax Act, 1961, after granting the Company an adequate opportunity of being heard. The matter can be referred to the Transfer Pricing Officer (TPO) only if the AO concludes that such undertaking qualifies as an international transaction under Section 92B of the Act. Consequently, the High Court set aside the draft assessment order and the TPO's order passed pursuant to the ITAT's remand directions. In response to subsequent queries raised by the tax authorities, the Company submitted its detailed responses. Thereafter, vide order dated September 24, 2025, the AO disposed of the Company's objections and referred the matter to the TPO. The TPO, vide order passed under Section 92CA of the Act dated December 2, 2025, proposed a transfer pricing adjustment of ₹6,27,07,932. Subsequently, the AO issued a draft assessment order dated December 19, 2025, which was received by the Company on December 22, 2025. The Company thereafter received the final assessment order dated January 27, 2026 passed under Sections 143(3) read with 144C(3) of the Act, wherein an addition of approximately ₹6.26 crore was made on account of fees relating to the corporate guarantee undertaking. Aggrieved by the said order, the Company filed an appeal before the Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeals) [CIT(A)]. Pursuant to the assessment order, a tax demand of ₹443.28 crore was raised by the AO. The Company has also filed a stay application before the AO and, vide order dated April 28, 2026, obtained a stay of demand until the disposal of the appeal by the CIT(A).

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The appeal pertains to Assessment Year (AY) 2010-11 and has been filed against the assessment order dated January 27, 2016 passed by the Assessing Officer under Section 143(3) read with Section 144C(13) of the Income-tax Act, 1961. In the said order, the Assessing Officer made, inter alia, a disallowance of Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) expenses and transfer pricing adjustments relating to the provision for Business Support Services. The order also included a transfer pricing adjustment in respect of the alleged international transaction arising from the provision of a corporate guarantee by the Company. The Company has challenged the aforesaid disallowance and transfer pricing adjustments in the appeal.
tax_litigation.status: The order was received by the Company on March 6, 2026. The Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeals) decided the issues relating to the disallowance of ESOP expenses, disallowance under Section 14A, disallowance under Section 40(a)(ia) in respect of commission, transmission and uplinking charges, and disallowance of software expenses in favour of the Company. The appellate authority directed the exclusion of functionally dissimilar comparables from the final set of comparables used for benchmarking the Company's international transactions. In respect of the transfer pricing adjustment arising from the alleged international transaction of providing a corporate guarantee, the matter has been remanded to the file of the Assessing Officer for fresh adjudication in accordance with the decision rendered in the Company's case for Assessment Year 2008-09.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: For Assessment Year (AY) 2018-19, the Company filed a writ petition under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India before the Hon'ble High Court seeking, inter alia, the issuance of a writ of certiorari for quashing the order dated August 30, 2024 passed by the Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle-05, under Section 148A(d) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, as well as the consequential notice issued under Section 148 of the Act on the same date initiating reassessment proceedings, together with all proceedings arising therefrom. During the pendency of the writ petition, the Assessing Officer issued a notice under Section 142(1) of the Act seeking certain information and details from the Company in connection with the reassessment proceedings.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax (Central Circle 05)
tax_litigation.status: The matter is currently pending adjudication before the Hon'ble High Court and the Assessing Officer. The writ petition is scheduled for hearing before the Hon'ble High Court on August 27, 2026. In the interim, the Assessing Officer passed an assessment order under Section 147 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, dated March 27, 2026, making an addition of approximately ₹2.99 crore. The assessment order records that, pursuant to the directions of the Hon'ble High Court in W.P.(C) No. 1509/2025, any demand arising from the assessment order shall not be given effect to until the final disposal of the writ petition by the High Court or until further orders are passed by the Court. Accordingly, the enforceability of the demand remains subject to the outcome of the pending writ proceedings before the Hon'ble High Court.
